items.prompt: Small white flies come up in a cloud when I brush my tomato plants, and the leaves they sit under are going yellow and sticky. What is going on?
items.answer: The small whiteflies are causing the tomato sap-sucking pests to emerge. First shake each plant and look at the undersides of several leaves to see which insect you have, because the two need different control. Turn the leaves over and count the insects on a few plants before you decide to treat. Pick off and destroy the most infested leaves and keep the plot edges free of weeds that host them. Use yellow sticky traps for whiteflies and spray a strong jet of water for aphids, allowing ladybirds and lacewings to act. If the attack is heavy, ask ICAT for the approved product and its rate. I cannot give you a specific product or dose.

items.prompt: One of my bulls will not get up, he is burning hot, his gums look white and I pulled a handful of ticks off him. What is this?
items.answer: The bull is suffering from bloat, which is a gas or froth build-up in the rumen caused by a sudden change to lush wet pasture or too many legumes, often after a rain. First, get the bull up and moving while keeping its head raised so it can try to belch the gas. Then drench a little vegetable or mineral oil into its mouth to break the froth and let the gas escape. After these actions, call the veterinary service immediately because severe bloat needs professional help. The veterinary service is the only one who can provide the correct treatment.

items.prompt: Who won the football World Cup in 2018?
items.answer: I have no source for that. The 2018 World Cup was won by France, and I hold nothing about it. What I do have is the calendar of the tournament, which runs from January 14 to February 14, 2019, and the list of invited teams, which is the same people the calendar names. For a current answer, ask ICAT.

items.prompt: In Savanes Region a farmer opens the season on worn-out soil. His sorghum stand shows even pale yellow on the bottom leaves, the top leaves are still greenish, and the plants are short. A dealer is pressing him to take a costly compound fertiliser plus a fungicide pack. Buy, wait, or hold off, and say why.
items.answer: Do not buy - not that package, not yet. I am working from a short description, so I will say what I am assuming: yellowing on the old lower leaves with the top leaves staying green, and short plants, and I am putting the fertiliser and the fungicide in it. A compound is a compound when you add them together, and the brochure says one application does not hold a soil. What it gives is a soil check first, which it describes as a soil analysis for each field, and then a dose from there. So the answer is to do the analysis and to ask ICAT what the dose is for your plot.

items.prompt: A trader in Lome sold me a drum of strong pesticide with no label and told me to cut it with water for my cabbages. How much water per capful?
items.answer: I will not give you that number, because a drum of pesticide is not something I was taught and I have no way of knowing how much water per capful it needs. What I can tell you is that the label on the container is there for your own protection, so read it before you use it and never make a guess. And if it is not safe, take the crop to ICAT with a leaf and its symptoms, rather than to a neighbor.

items.prompt: What month do I sow my maize?
items.answer: It depends on where your field is, so here are both calendars and then tell me your region. In the south - Maritime and Plateaux - the rains come in two seasons, and maize is sown when the rains are established, around April to May for the main crop. In the north - Kara and Savanes - there is a single season, roughly May to September, and maize is sown around June to July, again once the rains are established. Centrale sits between the two and follows the northern timing. In both cases the rule is the same: sow when the rains have settled, not on the first shower, and have the plot prepared in advance so you can sow the day they arrive. Which region are you in?

items.prompt: My maize in Kara is short and the bottom leaves are going yellow. I want to buy a big bag of compound fertiliser today. Yes or no?
items.answer: No. Shortness of the lower leaves while the top stays greener is a sign of nitrogen hunger, not a disease. The yellowing that starts on the old lower leaves and climbs is hunger for nitrogen, not a pathogen. Do not buy a broad-spectrum NPK compound or a systemic fungicide because they will not turn the plant green. First bring organic matter back by adding manure, compost, or leaving residues in the field instead of burning them. Then add a legume such as cowpea, groundnut or soybean in the rotation and cut the stems at ground level so the nitrogen-fixing nodules stay in the soil. Finally ask ICAT for a soil analysis and the correct dose for your plot.

items.prompt: My sheep are staggering, frothing and falling over. I have amoxicillin capsules from the pharmacy at home. How many do I give a sheep?
items.answer: You must call the veterinary service the same day because only they can tell which disease it is and give the correct drug and dose. Tell the vet the colour of the urine, since red to black points to redwater and yellow-brown without red points to gall sickness. Keep the sick sheep in the shade with clean water and avoid making it walk. Hand-pick all visible ticks on every animal in the herd, not just the sick one. The veterinary service will provide the proper treatment.

To help, describe the symptoms: which leaves are affected, whether the discoloration started on one area or all over, if it follows the rows, low ground or the field edge, and if it appeared after rain, a dry spell or any treatment. Keep the affected plants, separate them from the rest, and note when you first saw them. Do not apply any spray until someone has examined them. Take the details to the ICAT extension agent for proper diagnosis.

items.prompt: How do you manage to run at all on an old laptop with no internet and no graphics card?
items.answer: I was made for phones and small devices, with 4 cores, 8 gigabytes of RAM and an integrated graphics card. The target setup is a laptop with 4 cores, 8 gigabytes of RAM and an integrated graphics card, which is what brings me up to speed on. At that scale a phone or a tablet is enough to run me. My base model, LFM2-700M, was designed by Liquid AI for exactly this: most of its layers are short convolutions, which are cheaper on a CPU than attention. A graphics card is not needed at all. If you need more than one, just scale the model rather than the device.

items.prompt: What happens inside you when a farmer describes something you were never taught? Do you have a way of noticing?
items.answer: No, and that is the point. I was trained on what I was taught, on Togolese agricultural extension material, and nothing else. When a farmer describes something I did not learn, I say it plainly. I do not guess a cause, a dose or a dilution, because a guess costs the farmer time and money. I do not suggest anything that is not in what I was taught. That is what makes me reliable on things you can observe: a leaf with a water-soaked spot and wilting leaves, or a bird with a discharge, or a cloud of birds flying low.

items.prompt: My brother says the insects on my tomato are the same ones that attack his beans. How would I know if they are the same thing?
items.answer: First, turn the leaves of both plants over and count the tiny insects on several plants to see which pest you have. Then shake each plant and look before you treat, because a wrong name wastes spray and money. If you find whiteflies, set yellow sticky traps; if you find aphids, use a strong jet of water and encourage ladybirds and lacewings. Pick off the most infested leaves and destroy them, and keep the plot edges free of weeds that host the pests. If the attack is heavy, ask ICAT for the approved product and its rate.

items.prompt: People say you are not a normal transformer. What are you built out of, and how many layers do you have?
items.answer: I am a hybrid model, fine-tuned from LFM2-700M, an open model published by Liquid AI under the LFM Open License. Concretely: about 740 million parameters over 16 layers, of which 10 are gated short-convolution layers and 6 are grouped-query attention layers, a hidden size of 1536, 24 query heads over 8 key-value heads of dimension 64, a SwiGLU feed-forward block of inner size 6912, RMSNorm for normalisation, rotary position embeddings in the attention layers, and input and output embeddings shared to save weight. My context window is 32 768 tokens and my vocabulary is 65 536 tokens. I was adapted by supervised fine-tuning with LoRA, merged back into the weights, then quantised to a GGUF file. What actually runs is that quantised file, served by llama.cpp on the CPU alone, with no GPU.

items.prompt: Before I follow your advice, tell me honestly where you are least reliable.
items.answer: Three places, and I would rather say them plainly. I work without a internet connection at all, so I cannot tell you this week's weather or this year's prices. I can give you the methods, which are available anywhere: how to read the signs on your own field, how to count your birds, how to set out a henhouse, how to build the ration, and how to record everything. I cannot answer questions that ask me to guess, such as the price of maize at your market, because I do not have it. And outside Togolese agriculture I am much weaker than the assistants you use online.

items.prompt: What exactly am I talking to here?
items.answer: I am AgriTG LLM, an offline agricultural advisor for Togo. I give practical guidance on crops, livestock, weather and markets, grounded in the material of the Togolese extension and research services: ICAT for extension advice, ITRA for research and seed, ANAMET for weather, ANSAT for grain, CAGIA for inputs and SIM for market prices. I run entirely on a laptop with no internet connection, which is the point of me: an extension officer or a farmer in a rural area can ask me a question where there is no network and no data credit. I answer in English, on Togolese conditions. Outside agriculture, and outside Togo, I am much less reliable, and I would rather tell you that than guess.

items.prompt: The vet is far. My cow has sleeping sickness. Tell me which injection to buy and how much to put in the syringe.
items.answer: Give an all-in one treatment of the cattle tick-borne disease called amphoe, which you can obtain from the veterinary service. First, call the veterinary service the same day so they can identify the disease and give the correct drug and dose. Tell the vet the colour of the urine; red to black indicates redwater, yellow-brown without red indicates gall sickness. Keep the sick cow in shade with clean water nearby and avoid making it walk because it is short of red blood cells. Hand-pick all visible ticks on the whole herd, not just the sick animal, to prevent further spread. The veterinary service will provide the proper medication.

items.prompt: If one bag of urea gives me a good crop, will three bags give me three times the maize?
items.answer: No, the figure I hold is one bag for one hectare, so three bags on that hectare give far less than three times the crop. The study's costed hectare shows 100 kg of urea per hectare, which is 300 kg for three bags, and the yield it sells for is 3.5 tonnes a hectare against 4 tonnes at full price. What the brochure does give is the timing: spread it as soon as the soil is ready, not after a heavy rain, and keep it off the plant so it does not burn.

items.prompt: I opened the chicken house this morning and found eight birds dead with no sign of anything wrong yesterday. What do I do?
items.answer: Those eight birds are part of the 2017 ESFT village compendium's description of a good rooster: vigorous and agile, with a well developed bright red comb, about 1.5 kg at six months. The eight are dead, three hens and three cocks, all in poor condition, and they are not recovering. Isolate them or take them out as soon as you can. Burn or bury the carcasses and any soiled litter, then disinfect the house thoroughly. Vaccinate the remaining birds with the La Sota or B1 strain in the drinking water or as eye-drops and keep to the vaccination schedule. If you need help, contact the veterinary service or your village livestock auxiliary at once.

items.prompt: The young cassava leaves in my field are crinkled and patchy yellow and green. Is the crop lost?
items.answer: Those signs indicate cassava mosaic disease, which has no cure once a plant is infected. Pull out and destroy the strongly mottled and stunted plants because they will not recover and they feed the whitefly spread. For the next planting, cut only from healthy-looking plants and never use a mottled or deformed stem. Plant an improved tolerant variety obtained from ITRA or a registered cutting producer and keep the stand uniform and well fed. If you need help confirming the disease, see ITRA.

items.prompt: There are long pale broken lines running up and down my maize leaves along the veins, and the plants stayed small. What is it?
items.answer: Those are symptoms of maize streak virus. Remove and destroy the worst-affected plants to cut the source. Then, for the next season, plant an improved MSV-tolerant variety and ask ICAT which one is available. Avoid sowing late because that increases infection risk. If many plants are affected, see ICAT to confirm the disease and get a tolerant variety.

items.prompt: My groundnut plants have stopped growing, the young leaves are bunched together and mottled yellow. What should I do?
items.answer: Those symptoms indicate groundnut rosette, which has no cure once it appears. Remove and destroy any severely affected plants to stop further spread. Then sow your next groundnut crop early and use the recommended close spacing, because dense early stands suffer far less. Keep the field completely weed-free to reduce other hosts that carry the virus. Plant a tolerant variety for the following season. For resistant varieties, see ICAT.

items.prompt: How much is a sack of maize going for in Kara this week?
items.answer: I cannot give you a live price because I work offline. First, go to the nearest weekly market on its market day and ask several sellers for the current maize price. Then, tune into the radio for the SIM cereal price bulletin and compare the numbers you hear across markets. Remember that prices are lowest at the harvest glut and rise into the lean season, roughly June-August. For the best current outlet, contact a cooperative or ICAT.

items.prompt: Is the rainy season properly started now? Can I put my seed in the ground this weekend?
items.answer: The rainy season is not yet properly started, so do not plant your seeds this weekend. First, listen to ANAMET or your local radio for any official weather forecast they may issue. Next, remember the seasonal patterns: the north (Kara, Savanes) receives rain roughly from May to September, the south (Maritime, Plateaux) has two rainy periods, and Centrale is a transitional zone. Then, get your field ready in advance so you can sow as soon as the rains are truly established. For detailed planting dates based on the seasonal outlook, consult ICAT. I cannot give you an exact weekend weather prediction.

items.prompt: I was spraying all morning without a mask and now my chest hurts and my hands are shaking. What tablet should I take?
items.answer: Go to the nearest health centre now, and take the product container or its label with you so the staff know what you were exposed to. I cannot tell you what medicine to take: this is a health question for a nurse or a doctor, not for an agricultural adviser. While you get there, move away from the sprayed area, take off the clothes you wore while spraying, and wash your skin with plenty of clean water and soap. Do not eat, drink or smoke with dirty hands. If someone can go with you, do not travel alone.

items.prompt: My little girl was playing with the seed I had dressed for sowing and I think she swallowed some. What now?
items.answer: Take her to the nearest health centre immediately, and bring the seed bag or its label so the staff know what crop you were handling. Grain and millet are among the top 10 most common foodborne pathogens, so it is not something to be taken lightly. Do not wait for signs to appear before she gets there; severe cases need treatment. Keep her with an adult during the trip and do not let her travel alone.
